data.narrative:
Lumaril is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mark Elliot and Ben Duffield that has raised $12M to date. The target operates within a sector populated by 1 public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ) and 8 private peers including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics.

Stage-progression analysis was the applicable valuation method for this engagement. Using the $12M total raised as a proxy for implied post-money value and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A progression, this method yields a $30M valuation. Peer-median triangulation was not applicable due to insufficient narrow peer comparables—while 8 same-sector peers exist in the Robotics & Manufacturing universe, filtering to same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier subsets did not yield the three or more datapoints required for reliable median estimation. Broader sectoral medians were therefore excluded to avoid false precision.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, centered on $30M. The narrow methodological base—reliance on a single applicable approach—represents the primary valuation uncertainty. Additional clarity on Lumaril's specific market position within robotics (manufacturing automation, logistics, autonomous systems, etc.), its unit economics relative to staged peers, and runway against burn would strengthen conviction in any point estimate within this range.
